ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Canada Business Corporations Act (RSC 1985, c C-44), as amended; Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1), as amended; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (SC 2000, c 17) and Regulations (SOR/2002-184); Criminal Code (RSC 1985, c C-46), ss. 462.31 and 462.33; Special Economic Measures Act (SC 1992, c 17); Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (SC 2011, c 21); United Nations Act (SC 2000, c 27); Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the passport or identity card of each director, officer, shareholder and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner of oaths in the country of issue / Canada
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issuing country is a contracting party; otherwise consular legalization by the nearest Canadian diplomatic or consular mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of status / certificate of good standing for each corporate shareholder of the proposed Quebec corporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or competent companies authority in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus endorsed translation if not in English or French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the local incorporation agent and registered office service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Beneficial owner(s) or corporate board of directors, notarized before a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / consular legalization when executed outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each ultimate beneficial owner, signed before a notary or lawyer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, with apostille or consular legalization if signed outside Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against FINTRAC's Politically Exposed Persons (domestic and foreign) definitions under the PCMLTFA, the United Nations Consolidated List, Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List, and the OFAC SDN list as best-practice; enhanced due diligence where any individual holds or has held prominent public office in the last 5 years, has close family or associates, or transacts with sanctioned states; ongoing transactional monitoring and re-screening at least every 180 days; documentation of negative news and adverse media checks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online portal at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; for a federal equivalent, Corporations Canada NUANS Online at https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/corporations-canada
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Where incorporating under Quebec provincial law, the company name must be in French or contain a French component mandated by the Charter of the French Language; any non-French trade name requires a French equivalent to appear in the registry. Letters are limited to Latin script, Arabic numerals, periods, apostrophes, hyphens, and spaces; names must be distinguishable from all existing registered names and marks. Federal names permit English/French equivalence subject to bilingual regulatory practice.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the REQ rejects a name declaration, the applicant may file a written application for review with the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal; a further appeal may be made to the Tribunal administratif du Québec within 30 days. For federal name refusals, the proposed corporation may apply to the Director under the CBCA for reconsideration within 30 days and may thereafter seek judicial review in the Federal Court; in all cases a fresh NUANS/name declaration search and reservation fee is required before refiling.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for an international tax structuring consultancy, provided that a physical street address in Quebec is designated as the registered office, the address is not a post-office box, and the premises are accessible during business hours for service of process and document inspection. Shared or virtual executive offices are accepted by REQ when the provider agrees to receive mail and service; remote-only substance without a Quebec address is not permitted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5-10% estimated annual risk of unannounced inspection for a standard advisory corporation; this risk increases materially if UBO filings are incomplete, live transactions are conducted with high-risk jurisdictions, or FINTRAC supervision flags unusual client activity. The REQ and provincial authorities may conduct premises verification under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 3, 10–11, 54–55; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 10–13; Taxation Act (Québec), CQLR c I-3 (QST).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online one-stop digital counter of the Gouvernement du Québec.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de constitution (Articles of Incorporation) transmitted electronically, accompanied by the Declaration of Registered Office and Directors' Consents; issuance of the Attestation de constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow or deposit requirement. Shares may be issued for money, property or past services (QBCA ss. 54–55); authorized share capital is defined solely in the articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Corporation under the Business Corporations Act (Québec) is ratified; the Subscriber's subscription for 100 common shares is accepted, and the shares are allotted and issued against payment of CAD 100 credited to the corporate account. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [Address], Québec, and the CEO is authorized to file the notices of office with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed President/CEO, [Name] Treasurer, and [Name] Corporate Secretary until the next annual meeting, each executing banking resolutions, GST/QST registrations, and ancillary statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online name research and reservation module (Recherche de nom).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online Demande de réservation de nom stating up to three proposed corporate names in priority order. The registrar verifies distinctiveness under art. 12 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Obtain the Certificat de réservation de nom valid for 90 days and align the legal name with the trilingual or French form required for the articles.
required_dossiers: Three proposed names in priority order
NUANS report or REQ validation result, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an amended request with alternate designations or seek administrative review of the registrar's refusal under CQLR c P-44.1; a new reservation may be obtained without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — one-stop digital counter (CliquezAffaires / ARI portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the statutory questionnaire generating the Statuts de constitution. Specify the authorized share structure, restrictions on share transfers, number and residency of directors, and the municipal address of the registered office in Québec. Attach the name reservation certificate and directors' consents. Pay the filing fee online and transmit the dossier; the registrar examines conformity with the QBCA and issues the Attestation de constitution together with the NEQ.
required_dossiers: Declaration of registered office in Québec
Consent of each director (formulaire de consentement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar queries the file under art. 10 of the legal publicity act, submit a corrective Décision modificative or supplemental declaration within the stated deadline; on refusal, apply for judicial review before the Court of Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (corporate act; no governmental filing required except optional registry update).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting or adopt written resolutions in lieu of meeting. Ratify incorporation, fix registered office address, appoint officers, adopt By-law No. 1 (general corporate by-law), approve bank account resolutions, authorize issuance of share certificates, and authorize GST/QST and CRA registrations. Record minutes in the corporate records book.
required_dossiers: Directors' consents and share subscription list
Bank account opening forms and authorized signatory specimens
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If minutes or resolutions contain defects, adopt a corrective resolution at the next board meeting and restate the minutes; document the correction in the corporate register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec; Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) if hiring employees.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the CRA Business Number (BN) and register for corporate income tax, GST/HST, and payroll deduction accounts. Concurrently register with Revenu Québec for QST, and with CNESST for the employer assessment account. Attach the NEQ attestation and certificate of incorporation. Maintain separate bank records for GST/QST remittance.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and By-law No. 1
Registered office address and banking details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec rejects the application for missing identifiers, correct the BN/NEQ linkage online and resubmit; use the corporate registry extract as proof of legal existence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Occupation Permit and Professional Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (e.g., Ville de Montréal — Service des permis d'exploitation) and, for reserved tax-accounting services, Ordre des comptables professionnels agréés du Québec (CPA Order).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal permit d'exploitation or certificat d'occupation for the registered office location. If the firm holds out as providing public accountancy or reserved tax services, obtain a CPA practice permit including professional liability insurance and compliance with the Professional Code. Submit the lease and fire safety certificate with the application.
required_dossiers: Lease or proof of occupancy of the office
CNESST registration where employees are engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On refusal, correct zoning or compliance deficiencies and appeal to the municipal permit committee; for CPA permits, file a representation before the Order's permit committee and, if necessary, the Tribunal administratif du Québec.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (corporate legal publicity); Ordre des comptables professionnels agréés du Québec (professional practice of reserved tax-accounting acts); municipal permit authority for physical premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis de pratique professionnelle en cabinet CPA (if reserved acts performed) or municipal Permis d'exploitation / Certificat d'occupation for the registered office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / De minimis — office-based consultancy with no industrial facility; no mandatory EIA and no Déclaration d'activité under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment (CQLR c Q-2, r. 23) for premises used solely for professional services.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC permit thresholds triggered; effluent limited to domestic sanitary sewer discharge complying with municipal by-laws; office waste and paper must be removed by authorized carriers under the Regulation respecting landfilling and incineration of residual materials (CQLR c Q-2, r. 19); negligible volatile organic compound emissions from cleaning supplies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal fire safety service under the Quebec Fire Safety Code; structural/occupancy clearance under the Quebec Building Code for the leased commercial premises; CNESST registration for workplace health and safety with annual wage statement; accessibility clearance for public access areas if client meetings are held at the registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Revenu Québec - https://www.revenuquebec.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident foreign entity incorporating in Canada obtains a federal Business Number (BN) by registering online through the CRA Business Registration Online portal or by mailing Form RC1 for a GST/HST account, payroll account, and importing/exporting account. For Quebec-specific GST/HST and QST administration, the corporation must separately register with Revenu Québec (Form RM-1 or online via Revenu Québec's business registration service) to obtain a Quebec Establishment Number (NEQ) and QST number. Required information typically includes the certificate of incorporation, registered office address in Canada or Quebec, full director/officer details, a Canadian resident representative for service of process, and constitutional documents. The BN and QST registration are TIN-equivalents for corporate tax input tax credit, remittance, and cross-border compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box entity classification election. A Canadian business corporation is automatically taxed at the entity level under the Income Tax Act. Available elections include: section 85 corporate rollover on contributions of property; section 216 election by non-residents to file a net-basis return on Canadian rental income; sections 83(2)/83(2.1) capital dividend elections; amalgamation rollover under section 87; and Quebec provincial elections mirroring federal rollover provisions. Hybrid mismatch and anti-arbitrage restrictions apply under sections 18.4, 18.5, and 18.6 of the Income Tax Act, limiting aggressive cross-border structured payments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 CAD (small-supplier threshold on worldwide taxable supplies made in the last four consecutive calendar quarters; both federal GST/HST and Quebec QST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time continuous transaction control (CTC) clearance, API fiscal stamping, or immediate digital stamp duty exists at the federal or Quebec level. Invoices must comply with CRA and Revenu Québec information requirements under the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax, including vendor name and registration number, recipient details, date, description, and tax charged. Mandatory electronic filing and remittance applies under GST/HST for registrants with gross annual taxable supplies above C$1.5 million, and Quebec QST returns are generally required to be filed electronically through Revenu Québec's portal. Large businesses must retain electronic records and support digital audits, but there is no per-invoice government approval or clearance mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for exports under the Excise Tax Act applies to goods exported from Canada and to services supplied to non-residents that are not consumed or used in Canada. For ISIC 7020 tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory, 0% GST/QST applies when the supply is made to a non-resident corporation, the service is not performed for a person in Canada, and the service is not in respect of real property or tangible personal property located in Canada. The supplier must maintain adequate records demonstrating the non-resident status of the recipient, the place of supply, and the absence of Canadian use or enjoyment. Cross-border advisory services may also be zero-rated under the various special rules for supplies made to non-residents where the primary beneficiary is outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Form B13A or CBSA-approved electronic export declaration / Canadian Automated Export Declaration system)
Bill of lading or air waybill
Purchase order or service contract clearly identifying the non-resident recipient
Inward remittance certificate or corporate bank transfer statement evidencing offshore payment and FX repatriation
Relevant customs coding (HS for goods, NAICS / service description for advisory services)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reverse zero-rating if discharge-of-export evidence is deficient, incomplete, or fraudulent. Penalties include 25% of the misstated tax claimed as gross negligence penalty under Excise Tax Act section 285, plus accrued interest; civil reassessments can claw back refunds or input tax credits for up to four years (or longer in cases of misrepresentation). Criminal prosecution for knowingly making false statements may result in fines and imprisonment, and Quebec equivalents under the Tax Administration Act impose substantial monetary penalties and personal director liability for wilful participation in false refund claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange administration is not centralized in a dedicated FX-control agency, but the Department of Finance Canada, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) collectively oversee monetary policy, AML/CTF reporting, and bank solvency/liquidity for cross-border funds flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible under IMF Article VIII. Both current-account transactions (intra-entity fees, interest, royalties, management charges) and capital-account flows (equity injections, shareholder loans, portfolio investments) are free from exchange-control restrictions and are not subject to pre-approval, minimum holding periods, or repatriation limits. Profit remittance is not blocked by FX law; however, outbound dividends, interest, and royalties to non-residents incur Part XIII withholding tax at treaty and domestic rates, and the legal solvency test under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Quebec Business Corporations Act applies before any dividend payment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirements. Exporters may retain 100% of foreign-currency earnings, invoice in CAD or any freely-convertible currency, and maintain foreign-currency bank accounts with Canadian banks. There is no statutory timeline for conversion of export receipts into CAD; FX conversion is at the exporter's commercial discretion, subject to FINTRAC reporting for any cross-border wire transfer of CAD 10,000 or equivalent.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Non-Resident Business Operating Account / Escrow Account
Global Business Account / Capital Trust Escrow
International Business Banking Account / Escrow Settlement Account
Cross-Border Business Account / Legal Funds Escrow
Corporate Multi-Currency Account / Escrow Reserve Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Canada permits non-bank fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) to operate as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC, but such entities cannot accept deposits or provide retail lending without holding a bank or trust-company license under the Bank Act or Provincial Trust and Deposit legislation. Freestanding foreign digital EMIs (e.g., Revolut, Wise) may offer cross-border payment, FX conversion, and card issuance through Canadian MSB registration, but a Schedule I bank account is required for rigorous treasury control, capital escrow, and trade-related outbound clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banks do not impose a universal statutory requirement for directors to appear physically. Remote onboarding is available for Canadian-resident directors via video-verified KYC and digital identity authentication. For non-resident directors, enhanced due diligence commonly mandates: (i) certified copy of passport/ID, (ii) notarized corporate resolutions, (iii) banking references, and (iv) sometimes a branch visit or acceptance of a signed and witnessed KYC questionnaire. Best practice for a Quebec incorporated consultancy is to arrange in-person or notarized interviews for all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) to avoid onboarding delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO resident in a high-risk or sanctioned jurisdiction (e.g., FATF grey-list country) or beneficial owner appears in a politically exposed persons (PEP) database.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide corporate organigram and certified registry extracts from Registraire des entreprises du Québec and/or Corporations Canada; independent PEP status justification; source-of-wealth statement supported by audited financial statements, tax returns, bank references, and a legal opinion confirming legitimate source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border transaction velocity inconsistent with a low-risk consultancy (e.g., fees > CAD 200,000/month routed through multiple non-Canadian payment gateways).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present executed client engagement agreements, itemized invoices, tax structuring deliverables, transfer-pricing analysis, and a treasury cash-flow forecast; provide board resolution showing operational and tax rationale; secure a third-party AML assessment to match sector-specific activity profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disbursements to opaque jurisdictions for trade/consulting services, especially where the receiving country is a non-FATF-member jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For each disbursement, retain underlying contracts (ISIC 7020 scope), deliverables acceptance evidence, independent valuation benchmarking, and legal documentation validating cross-border tax structuring purpose; record end-beneficiary details and transaction-level compliance with FINTRAC 'Know Your Client' rules; implement a subsidiary-ledger segregation of trust vs operational funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed third-party funding of the capital injection, capital used to obscure tax liability, or conflicting data between corporate records and bank account details.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compile a full source and use-of-funds declaration; certified UBO ownership chain; clear professional-engagement letter signed by ultimate tax client; independent accountant attestation that the entity is not a shell; evidence of Quebec economic substance (office, bank, director's address, active licences) to substantiate legitimate tax structuring.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound subscription proceeds from foreign parent shareholders or investors should be routed via the SWIFT network with standard Correspondent Banking messages. For payment purpose codes, use 'D' (Direct Investment) or 'G' (Equity Capital) in the SWIFT remittance field; although Canada does not assign mandatory FX purpose codes, FINTRAC requires a report for each international electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more. To verify the legal origin, the receiving Canadian bank will ask for the payment instruction, corporate authorization (board resolution), tax identification number of the remitter, a copy of the signed subscription/funding agreement and the Quebec corporate registry attestation showing issuance of shares or shareholder loan documentation. Routing should be direct through the bank's correspondent network to avoid intermediary banks that might reject the 'capital injection' wording; do not commingle operational revenue with capital funding in the same message.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and consulting disbursements are performed primarily through SWIFT MT103 (Customer Transfer) for straightforward cross-border fee payments, which must contain the legal entity identifiers, client reference, and clear invoice number. For larger procurement or mandates requiring documentary security, a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) is the standard clearing rail, issued pursuant to UCP 600, with the Canadian bank confirming the applicant's commitment. For recurring international tax-consulting invoices, an MT103 is the most efficient rail, accompanied by a digital copy of the invoice and signed engagement. Disbursements to Quebec and intra-group accounts can be cleared through Interac e-Transfer for small amounts or EFT via the Canadian automated clearing system (ACSS) for CAD; foreign-currency payables (USD/EUR) are cleared via correspondent banking or SWIFT RGP (Real-Time Gross Settlement) equivalents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX Forward Contracts (CAD against USD, EUR, GBP, JPY) to lock manage consulting fee conversion flows
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies lacking active onshore delivery (e.g., certain emerging-market currencies) to hedge cross-border exposure without settling the principal
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) for matched funding and multi-year tax-structuring fee settlements
Vanilla Currency Options (FX Calls/Puts) for contingent capital injections, cross-border acquisitions, or treasury advisory engagements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal annual return under Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA s.263.1) — confirmation of registered office, directors and share capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the annual anniversary of federal incorporation or continuation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late-filing tolerance; two consecutive missed annual returns may lead to administrative dissolution by Corporations Canada. An inactive return also impairs issuance of compliance certificates and bank/professional licensing diligence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec annual declaration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (c. P-44.1) — current directors, registered office, share capital and persons with significant control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the registration anniversary date established by REQ; the online filing window generally opens 30 days before that anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an administrative penalty after the REQ reminder; persistent default for two consecutive years can lead to radiation (cancellation) of registration and eventual administrative dissolution of the corporation. Directors may become personally liable for obligations arising during the default period.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A CBCA non-distributing (private) corporation may avoid an auditor by unanimous shareholder consent for the financial year. Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, a non-issuing corporation may similarly dispense with an audit by unanimous shareholder waiver; an audit is mandatory for any reporting issuer, public distribution of securities, or if shareholders validly request the appointment of an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises and reporting issuers; Canadian ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook – Part II) or IFRS for private enterprises; accounting standards applied must be consistent and disclosed in the financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For CBCA corporations, an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) Register must be maintained and updated within 10 business days after a share transfer or any change to a controlling individual. Quebec's annual declaration requires a current confirmation of share capital and persons with significant control. Any shareholding transfer during the year must be entered in the Register of Members and, where applicable, the ISC register before the federal annual return and Quebec annual declaration are filed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC/UBO)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 18,000 per annum for a full certified audit; USD 2,000 - 5,000 for a review engagement if the audit has been waived

stage_6.entry_description: Legal name, business number (BN), fiscal year-end, home office jurisdiction, type (CCPC/non-CCPC).
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations use the same T2 form/BN; select applicable treaty article; a non-resident without a BN must register through CRA, and may use the streamlined T2S where eligible.
